Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 6225 -1971 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SHIFTS OVAL EYE PLATES 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by tlic Indian Standards Institution 
on 23 August 1971, after the draft finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and 
Packaging Division Cofuncil. 

0.2 Eye plates arc provided on the topmost deck and at other decks as 
required, to secure guy ropes from masts, derrick posts, etc. 

0.3 Eye plates arc provided with the sole plates to strengthen and increase 
the contact area and are cither directly riveted to deck or weldc^ to the 
deck. 

0.4 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been deri>«rd from 
DIN 82025 'Oval eye plates', issued by Deutsche! Nornienausschuis. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular rcquircmenc of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or cakulated, express- 
ing the result of a test or analysis, sliall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifics the material and dimensions for ship's oval eye 
plates. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definition shall apply. 

2.1 Safe Worlcutg Load — The safe working load of the eye plate is the 
maximum tensile load likely to occur in the guy ropes attached to it. If 



*Rules for rounding off numerical values {rtvistd). 



IS : «225 * 1971 

more than one rope is secured to the eye plate, the sum of the maximum 
tensile load on each of the rope, is the safe working load of the oval eye 
plate. 

3. MATERIAL 

3.1 Ship^s oval eye plates shall be made from any of the follovvinf» 
material: 

a) Carbon steel forgings conforming to IS : 326 1-1 966*. 

b) Structural steel conforming to IS : 3039-19651. 

4- TYPES 

4»1 Oval eye plates shall be of two types, namely, lypc A and Type B, as 
shown in Table K 

4*2 Type A eye plates are suitable for attachment to drrks, bulworks, etc. 
Type B eye plates are suitable for attachment to derricks, 

5. SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

5.1 The shape and dimensions of the ship's oval eye plates together with 
sole plate shall be as given in Table 1. 

6. TOLERANCES 

6.1 The tolerances on other dimensions shall be of roarsc series according 
toIS:2102^1969t 

7. MARKING 

7.1 Each oval eye plate shall be marked legibly and indelibly with the 
manufacturers identification mark, and the safe working load. 

7J.1 Oval eye plates may also be marked with the ISI Certification 
Mark* 

Note ~ The u»c of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marb ) Act. and the Rules and Uegutations 
made thereunder. Picscnce of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements 
of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection , testing and quality control 
during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated 
by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are 
continuously checked by ISI for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, 
under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to 
manufacture! 9 or pro€cs8oni» may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution*

'(Specification for structural steel ( shipbuilding quality ), 

I Allowable deviations for dimensions without specified tolerances (first nvism ).
